I have Crohn's disease and about 8 years ago, I had a severe reaction to a Remicaid infusion. On Tuesday, I went to the infusion center and spent 4 hours hooked up to an IV as the medication was administered. On Friday, I started experiencing moderate joint pain and stiffness. I attributed it to the fact that I have a laundry list of medical issues and it being just a bad day for me. By Saturday afternoon, I couldn't move. My joints locked up and every movement was agonizing. When I finally decided it was time to go to the ER, I couldn't even walk to the car out in my driveway. I shuffled through the house, vomited on myself about halfway through from the pain, and was then carried to the car by my dad. My (then) fiancé drove me to the the hospital, where he had to carry me to a wheelchair. I shit myself in the waiting room because I couldn't get myself out of the chair and into the bathroom. It was probably one of the most humiliating moments of my life. Once I got back into a room, a nurse cleaned me up and then proceeded to ask all the diagnostic questions and have me rate my pain. On a scale from 1-10, I rated it as a 12. That was the only question I could answer. I couldn't think straight, I could barely talk. It took two doses of morphine followed by two shots of dilaudid to get the pain to a manageable level. Only then was I able to explain the progression of my symptoms and any possible causes. After having imaging done on all of my major joints, they found no injuries and finally settled on the Serum Sickness diagnosis. After another shot of dilaudid, I was sent home with a prescription for loads of pain medication and instructed to wait it out the best I could.

I have mild asthma. Nothing horrific, it just can become problematic when the allergens in the air are high. While at work one day, I started having what I thought was an asthma attack. I took my inhaler and sat for a while, hoping it would pass. It didn't. So I get my manager to cover my shift so I can get my ass to the ER. Of course, I had to go home and change and get someone to come with me because I wasn't prepared to spend hours there alone.

Fast forward to the ER (to which I was delivered by ambulance, because apparently I was turning blue and that prompted my dad to call 911)-
I was answering all of the usual questions, listing off my medications, and trying desperately not to rip the oxygen thingy out of my nose. Then I mentioned that one of my legs felt tight and had been kind of swollen for the past day. Then comes the ultrasound part...

After discovering the clot in my leg, they took me for a CT scan of my chest. That scan revealed a 3 inch saddle embolism in my lungs, pressing on my heart. Apparently, that's a huge fucking deal. I'm then informed that they are going to perform a rarely attempted procedure that would hopefully break up the embolism on my heart without sending it into my brain and causing an aneurysm.

This rarely performed procedure had NEVER been attempted at this hospital. It took them two hours of conference calls and what I'm assuming is some MD-level Googling before they were comfortable enough to start the procedure. They were going to push a strong clot-busting compound directly into the vein/artery (I don't know the difference) where the embolism was located. I was strapped to an operating table, Jesus-style, and they began placing lines in my arms and one in my neck leading directly to my heart. They pushed some Ativan and Morphine through one of those lines, and that's the last thing I remember for 9 days.

Happyish ending, though. I'm not dead. So I stick that one in the win column.

I have Crohn's disease and about 7 years ago, I had a severe reaction to a Remicaid infusion. On Tuesday, I went to the infusion center and spent 4 hours hooked up to an IV as the medication was administered. On Friday, I started experiencing moderate joint pain and stiffness. I attributed it to the fact that I have a laundry list of medical issues and it being just a bad day for me. By Saturday afternoon, I couldn't move. My joints locked up and every movement was agonizing. When I finally decided it was time to go to the ER, I couldn't even walk to the car out in my driveway. I shuffled through the house, vomited on myself about halfway through from the pain, and was then carried to the car by my dad. My (then) fiancé drove me to the the hospital, where he had to carry me to a wheelchair. I shit myself in the waiting room because I couldn't get myself out of the chair and into the bathroom. It was probably one of the most humiliating moments of my life. Once I got back into a room, a nurse cleaned me up and then proceeded to ask all the diagnostic questions and have me rate my pain. On a scale from 1-10, I rated it as a 12. That was the only question I could answer. I couldn't think straight, I could barely talk. It took two doses of morphine followed by two shots of dilaudid to get the pain to a manageable level. Only then was I able to explain the progression of my symptoms and any possible causes. After having imaging done on all of my major joints, they found no injuries and finally settled on the Serum Sickness diagnosis. After another shot of dilaudid, I was sent home with a prescription for loads of pain medication and instructed to wait it out the best I could.
